articleTitle: Attentive Feature Segmentation model for Stroke detection on MRI images
abstract: Medical image segmentation plays a crucial role in treatment planning, disease diagnosis, and guiding surgical navigation. Research should focus on medical image segmentation to achieve substantial breakthroughs or fill knowledge gaps that could lead to discoveries and improvements. Deep learning (DL) techniques have recently become necessary in creating advanced models, particularly for medical image segmentation. This paper introduces a novel segmentation algorithm specifically designed for MRI images. Initially, the paper will discuss the introduction and challenges in medical image segmentation. Later, developing a novel attentive feature-based segmentation algorithm is focused and their corresponding evaluation steps are measured. The evaluation metrics are finally compared with other existing segmentation algorithms and concluded that the proposed model surpasses the cutting-edge methods by notable differences in performance, showing the adaptability and overall effectiveness of the proposed model.

articleTitle: Progress and Perspectives of Augmentative and Alternative Communication in the Indian Context
abstract: This paper presents novel approach to augmentative and alternative communication (AAC) within the Indian context, focusing on Indian Sign Language (ISL) recognition. The proposed idea integrates a sensor-equipped glove system and utilizes an inertial measurement unit (IMU) to capture and analyze precise hand movements essential for ISL communication. By leveraging wearable sensor technology, our approach aims to provide real-time interpretation of ISL gestures, enabling individuals with communication impairments to effectively convey their messages. The integration of IMU technology ensures accurate tracking of hand movements, enhancing the overall reliability and usability of the system. This innovative solution has the potential to significantly improve communication accessibility for the ISL community in India, fostering greater inclusion and participation in various social and educational settings.

articleTitle: Experimental Analysis on Optical Properties of Nanofluids used for Solar applications
abstract: The use of Nano fluids in solar thermal energy systems represents a significant advancement that can enhance performance, reduce costs, and contribute to a more sustainable energy future. Nano fluids are used in solar collectors, concentrated solar power to improve the performance. Understanding the optical properties of Nanofluids is crucial, as these properties affect how well the Nanofluids absorb, transmit, or scatter solar radiation. High absorptivity and low emissivity are desirable characteristics for Nanofluids used as direct solar absorbers in solar thermal engineering applications. In this study, Graphene Nano particles (GNPs) at concentrations ranging from 0.3% to 1.2% by weight were added to distilled water for the preparation of Nano fluids. The Nanofluids were prepared using a trans-o-probe sonicator and stabilized with Cetyl trimethyl ammonium bromide (C-TAB). Their optical properties were measured using a UV-VIS spectrophotometer. The results reveal that absorbance values significantly increased with the addition of nanoparticles to the water. Absorbance values rose from 0.46 to 0.86 as the concentration of nanoparticles increased from 0.3% to 1.2% by weight. These developed Nanofluids are suitable for use as solar absorbers in solar collectors, solar desalination, and solar heating systems.

articleTitle: Leveraging MFCs for Bioenergy in Sensor Technologies
abstract: Microbial Fuel Cells (MFCs) are an innovative technology that combines bioremediation and bioenergy generation. This study focuses on developing an MFC system, with particular attention to laboratory tests of different MFC designs. The main goal is to identify an efficient design that can both generate power and treat water effectively. The study explores the ability of MFCs to generate electricity, specifically for powering sensors from soils, sediments, and wastewater, which can be applied in real-world scenarios. The main objective is to examine how the amount of organic matter in a sample affects the electricity production of MFCs. The results show that samples with more organic matter produce more electricity when used to power MFCs. The study also looks at the temperature range that is most effective for MFC operation by measuring its thermal limits.Over a 10-day period, there is a nearly linear decline in power production from the MFCs. The second objective is to find the best conditions for MFCs to maximize electricity generation. A comparison of different conditions and sample types, including benthic mud, sewage water, and agricultural soil, is conducted. The experiment shows that the benthic mud sample, which contains more organic matter, produces more electricity than the other two samples. The study concludes that selecting the right sample type, temperature, and chamber size can improve the electricity generation of MFCs.

articleTitle: A Portable Solar Charging System for Electric Bicycles and Batteries
abstract: This is the reason behind cars becoming electrified, owing to environmental pollution. In fact, if fossil fuels get converted into electric energy and supply it to the battery or electric vehicles, it will not reduce air pollution; it is just a change in the kind of energy being used. Since EVs are renewable, sustainable, and not very harmful to the environment, it is thus better to feed them power. This paper introduces a comprehensive portable solar charging system that uses renewable energy to efficiently charge electric bicycles and batteries. The system consists of foldable solar panels, a photo voltaic charge controller and a DC-DC boosting converter., which offers a sustainable and eco-friendly power generation solution for EVs and batteries. For better efficiency, the MPPT algorithm is used. With the assistance of MATLAB simulations, this new system not only encourages the use of clean energy sources but also offers a versatile charging solution for a variety of small and medium electrical applications. This contribution marks an important step toward sustainable transportation and advancing the use of renewable energy sources, thereby assisting worldwide efforts to prevent the harmful effects of global warming and reduce air pollution.

articleTitle: Improved Virtual Impedance Droop for Different Loads
abstract: Droop-based solutions have been widely utilized to regulate voltage source inverters in microgrids that are powered by distributed generation units. The benefits of this technique have been extensively explored, but its implications on the power quality and stability of microgrid based inverters have not been well investigated. An inverter can be set by introducing a Virtual Impedance, which simulates an additional impedance in the actual physical circuit, between the inverter and the load. An improved virtual impedance control approach is suggested to solve the problem of unbalanced and harmonic power sharing among parallel inverters caused due to mismatch of feeder impedance in islanded microgrids. Employed an improved virtual impedance droop management technique to enhance stability and power distribution. To validate the proposed approach, simulations are implemented in MATLAB/SIMULINK tools.

articleTitle: Designing of a TEG module for Domestic purpose in Remote tribal Area in Odisha
abstract: The population is increasing in a vigorous rate and Technology is getting advanced. However, still larger populations are away from electricity. These populations lack access to basic lighting during night time. Transmission line is not commissioned to their location. Even though the solar energy is suitable, but due to environmental conditions, these are not much popular. The tribal people cannot afford the other renewable energy due to cost issue. For the above issues the thermos electric generator is an optimum solution. In this research a domestic TEG module is designed to provide a continuity of electricity for tribal community in Odisha. The simulation is being performed using MATLAB based environment. The detailed modeling is provided for a complete understanding about the topic. The operation is verified under different scenarios. The observations are noted for determining the efficacy of the system and gauging the feasibility. The research work will be helpful for the researcher working in this field.

articleTitle: Revolutionizing Retail with Touchless Cart Technology Through Gesture-Controlled Shopping
abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic brought the demand for non-contact technologies to the next level in high-traffic areas such as supermarkets, where physical contact should be minimized for hygiene and safety. Grand View Research projects the global touchless sensing industry will reach a size of USD 15.3 billion by 2027. This project thus presents a fully non-contact solution for shopping based on both digit and alphabetic gesture recognition technology. Custom trained CNN model on the American Sign Language (ASL) dataset is used to make real-time hand gesture recognition able to select items, specify quantities, and place orders without touching carts or checkout terminals by making simple hand movements. It processes the hand gestures with great accuracy-93% accuracy on the custom dataset which recognizes both digits (0-9), as well as alphabets from A-Z. Real-time visual feedback and gesture validation with animated confirmation loops are the strengths of this system and lessen errors due to intuitive interaction with the user. The system is designed to be accessible for users with disabilities while also targeted to future voice command interfaces. Future improvements include broadened categories of products, wider gesture recognition, and integration with vending machines. This is an innovative hygienic shopping experience using practical applications of machine learning and computer vision through custom gesture recognition.

articleTitle: Optimized Nearest Store allocation using Dijkstra’s and Bellman-Ford Algorithms for Enhanced Retail Efficiency
abstract: In the rapidly evolving landscape of retail, the demand for personalized and efficient shopping experiences is paramount. This project introduces an advanced Nearest Store Allocator System, leveraging the power of Dijkstra’s algorithm for minimum distance and Bellman-Ford algorithm for handling complex graph structures to determine the closest store based on user-inputted search items. By employing two comprehensive datasets—Item List and Location List—the system integrates vast location information crucial for processing through these algorithms. The dual-algorithm approach ensures swift and accurate identification of all potential stores within a user-specified range, optimizing store allocation and significantly enhancing customer satisfaction. Through comparative analysis, this study identifies the most efficient algorithm suitable for real-time store location tasks. The implementation of this system not only promises homogeneous service delivery but also underscores the importance of algorithmic efficiency in contemporary retail management. This research aims to provide a robust framework that can be extended to various applications, ultimately contributing to a seamless and enriched shopping experience for consumers.

articleTitle: Superconductors Application in Power Sector: A Review
abstract: This study investigates the use of high-temperature superconductors (HTS) in the power industry, starting with the historical discovery of superconductors. It highlights the distinct features of HTS, including zero electrical resistance and perfect diamagnetism. The focus is on Yttrium Barium Copper Oxide (YBCO), Bismuth-Strontium-CalciumCopper-Oxide (Bi-2223), and Magnesium Diboride (MgB2), exploring their impact on power transmission efficiency, transformer innovations, and Superconducting Magnetic Energy Storage (SMES) systems. The paper also examines the economic viability and environmental sustainability of these materials in transforming the power sector, addressing challenges and future opportunities for widespread adoption.

articleTitle: Effects of Air Density Parameters in Modelling Power Curve of a Wind Turbine with Artificial Neural Network
abstract: In recent years, the installed capacity of wind power plants (WPP) has rapidly increased due to supportive policies and decreased installation costs in many countries. In this context, ensuring the optimum operating condition of WPPs is related to energy efficiency. The energy efficiencies of WPPs are determined using the power curves of wind turbines (WT) in the field. This situation has increased the need for an exact assessment of WT power curves. In this study, the wind speed, wind direction, output power, air temperature, and air pressure data are obtained from a WT in Türkiye at 10-minute intervals over a year. An artificial neural network (ANN) model trained in the Neural Designer software tool used these data. Two different combinations were composed for input. Firstly, the wind speed and direction data are used for input layers. Secondly, air pressure and temperature data are also added to input layers. The output layer is the WT power output. The first and second model goodness of fit (R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>) values are 0.990 and 0.993, respectively. The second model mean squared error (MSE), root mean squared error (RMSE), and normalized squared error (NSE) have minimum values. These results show that the containing air press data method can used as a more reliable tool for WT power output.

articleTitle: Sophisticated Machine Learning Methods to Improve Named Entity Identification in Historical English Text
abstract: Named Entity Identification (NEI) in historical English texts poses great challenges because of archaic language systems, inconsistent spellings, and varied contexts. Traditional strategies frequently conflict with accuracy and contextual expertise, leading to suboptimal overall performance in extracting significant entities from these texts. This examine proposes a singular method using a RoBERTa-BiLSTM hybrid version to decorate NEI effectiveness. By leveraging the contextual embeddings from RoBERTa and the sequential processing skills of Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (BiLSTM), the proposed approach objectives to improve entity recognition in ancient files. The methodology includes the collection of a numerous corpus of historical English texts, accompanied with the aid of preprocessing steps which include tokenization and normalization. The version is trained and evaluated the use of trendy metrics, demonstrating brilliant outcomes: an accuracy of 92.37%, precision of 93.71%, consider of 92.9%, and an F1 rating of 91.06%. These findings imply an extensive development over present methods, showcasing the efficacy of the RoBERTa-BiLSTM framework in addressing the complexities of NEI in historical contexts. This study contributes to the field of computational linguistics by way of providing a sturdy answer for named entity identity in texts that are often neglected via present day models.

articleTitle: Quantization Noise Analysis of Rounding and Truncation Methods for Sinusoidal Signals
abstract: Quantization noise is an problem in converting an analog signal to digital and there are two methods called as Rounding and Truncation to minimize the error during the digitization process. The behavior of quantization noise depends on the components of the sinusoidal signal and the conditions under which the conversion process takes place. This paper presents an analysis of the behavior of quantization noise for a sinusoidal signal. Computer simulation to quantize on the sinusoidal input signal is done using the Rounding and Truncation methods. Signal to quantization noise ratio (SQNR) comparisons for the Rounding and Truncation methods of quantization error is done for a sinusoidal signal. For selected quantization bit rates from 3-bit to 16-bit, the SQNR is calculated using the formula and then simulation is performed to determine the SQNR using the Truncation method and Rounding method. According to simulation results, it has been observed that there is difference of about 5 dB between SQNR error using the formula and the SQNR using the Rounding for quantization error. Similarly, it has been observed that there is difference of about 6 dB between the SQNR error using the formula and the SQNR using the Truncation for quantization error. It has also been observed that there is difference of about 1 dB between the SQNR quantization errors using the Truncation and using the Rounding.

articleTitle: Economic Load Dispatch Problem Using Different Metaheuristic Algorithms
abstract: Economic Load Dispatch (ELD) is the technique of dividing power volumes to the generators in the mix so that the system load can be delivered efficiently and effectively. It involves the distribution of generation output among multiple power plants while minimizing the overall cost of generation. Optimization is a mathematical strategy to calculate the maxima or minima of any functions in a selected region. Several optimization approaches compete for the optimal answer. One such approach is the use of the Grey Wolf Optimization algorithm (GWO) that based on the Grey Wolf hierarchy and hunting scheme. To assess GWO’s reliability, a comparison was made to a few metaheuristic techniques. The ‘GWO’ is compared to ‘Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO)’, ‘Sine Cosine Algorithm (SCA)’ and ‘Turbulent Flow of Water Optimization (TFWO)’. The objective is to examine and determine which of the aforementioned algorithms is the most effective and can handle complex constraints and nonlinear cost functions in ELD problems, ultimately leading to a more reliable power dispatch solution and most cost-efficient.

articleTitle: Using Cutting-Edge Natural Language Processing Techniques to Enhance Essay Grading Algorithms
abstract: Essay grading is one of the most cumbersome tasks that, so far, have depended on human scores to evaluate linguistic proficiency, coherence, and argumentation. Yet this work aims to present an alternative way of addressing the automation of essay grading based on advanced techniques of NLP. In more detail, it utilizes a hybrid deep learning model that combines BERT with LSTM networks to capture semantic understanding and sequential context in student essays. Use BERT to extract rich contextual embeddings allowing for deeper text understanding, then further process them with LSTM for retaining long dependencies while offering strong predictions. It learns subtle nuances in how essays should be graded along dimensions such as grammar, coherence, or argumentation structure by learning from a dataset of student essays graded by human experts. This approach indicates significant improvement in grading accuracy beyond traditional machine learning models and offers more reliable and scalable solutions for automated essay scoring. Thus, BERT-LSTM displays high performance in the rating task of essays with minimal or no human interference in the case of the minority class as it reduces bias and maintains consistency in diverse topics and writing styles. The research contribution will be onto this newly emerging field of educational technology, providing an innovative tool that enhances the efficiency of grading an essay fairly and, therefore, supports educators and improves learning outcomes for students.

articleTitle: FPGA-Driven Analysis of 9's and 10's Complement Circuits: Power and Thermal Insights on Kintex Board
abstract: As advanced electronics and computing systems are designed, more digital systems that operate with low energy become in great demand making circuit designs that are more energy-saving and conducive to use indispensable. This paper is concerned with the synthesis and realization of the complement of nine and ten arithmetic circuits on the Kintex FPGA board, concerning thermal management and energy efficiency. The 9s complement consumes a total power of 1.499W whereas the 10s complement consumes 1.665W. Additionally, thermal analysis indicated that thermal heat margins of 72.4°C for the 9s complement and 72.1°C for the 10s complement were realized. Therefore, these results imply that the Kintex FPGA could be used as a power-affordable platform for digital hardware designs to meet the green communication objectives without compromising the hardware functionality and power performance.

articleTitle: Real-Time Facial Expression Recognition Using Deep Learning for Enhanced Human-Machine Interactions
abstract: Real-time facial emotion recognition is a rapidly advancing field in computer vision and artificial intelligence with wide-ranging applications. This project implements a system for detecting and classifying facial expressions in real-time video streams using deep learning techniques. A convolutional neural network (CNN) model was developed and trained on the FER-2013 dataset to recognize seven basic emotions: anger, disgust, fear, happiness, sadness, surprise, and neutral. The system architecture integrates face detection, facial landmark extraction, and emotion classification components. Data augmentation and preprocessing techniques were applied to improve model performance. Two CNN architectures were evaluated - a baseline model and an enhanced model with additional layers and data augmentation. The enhanced model achieved 75.97% accuracy on the test set, surpassing the current state-of-the-art for the FER-2013 dataset. A graphical user interface was developed using Python Tkinter to create an accessible application. Real-time testing demonstrated the system’s ability to detect faces and classify emotions in live video feeds from a webcam. The system shows promise for applications in fields such as human-computer interaction, security, marketing, and mental health monitoring.

articleTitle: Facial Emotion Detection Using DeepFace
abstract: Facial emotions are the most important signals of our face as they tell us about an individual’s personality, feelings, motives, or intentions. Emotion detection offers a wide range of applications in human-computer interaction, healthcare, target advertising, education, and many more. This paper explores the use of DeepFace for facial emotion detection. DeepFace is a deep learning facial recognition and facial attribute analysis library which has pre-trained models. The performance is evaluated for static images, multi-face images, and in real-time integrated with user feedback to achieve better accuracy. DeepFace also identifies multi-faces in images and in real-time. We employ OpenCV and DeepFace analyzer for face detection and emotion detection. This model also gives the confidence scores in percentages of detected emotion labels. We achieved an accuracy of 84.62% for real-time with user feedback, 73.33% for static images and 55.55% for multi-face images.

articleTitle: Empowering Rural Communities: Feasibility and Optimization of Hybrid Renewable Energy Systems for Sustainable Electricity Using HOMER Software
abstract: Rural India faces rising energy needs. The challenges that come with dependence on traditional grid electricity show a clear need for sustainable energy options. This case study looks at Khajuri-Motihani, a village located in the Saharsa District of Bihar. Here, the main source of energy comes from the grid, provided by North Bihar Power Distribution Company Limited. A Hybrid Energy System (HES) that combines solar photovoltaic (PV) panels & wind energy is suggested. This plan aims to boost local energy production & self-sufficiency. Using the Hybrid Optimization Model for Electric Renewables (HOMER) software, the possible setups of this hybrid system was explored. The analysis is tailored to specific resources available at the site & load demands. The goal of this study is to design the system in a way that reduces both the net present cost (NPC) & the standardized cost of energy (COE). The study also wants to maximize the use of renewable energy while cutting carbon emissions. By conducting a detailed techno-economic analysis, assessed how different mixes of solar & wind resources perform under various operational strategies. The findings show that creating Khajuri-Motihani as a renewable energy hub is practical. This approach could serve as a model for other rural communities in India that want to shift towards sustainable & resilient energy systems. Overall, this research adds to the larger conversation about integrating renewable energy in areas with fewer resources. It helps promote energy independence along with environmental sustainability.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of PEM Fuel cell using COMSOL
abstract: This paper investigates the performance characteristics of Polymer Electrolyte Membrane Fuel Cells (PEMFCs) under varying operating conditions. Emphasizing the importance of temperature, electrolyte conductivity, and reactant mole fractions, the study utilizes a single passage twisting configuration modeled in COMSOL. Results reveal that increasing operating temperatures enhances cell performance, with optimal performance observed near the gas humidification temperature. The study also highlights the relationship between the mole fractions of hydrogen and oxygen and their effects on electrochemical reaction rates, indicating that high hydrogen concentrations improve output power but may lead to flooding issues. Furthermore, it is shown that relative humidity plays a critical role in proton conductivity, with excessive dryness at elevated temperatures diminishing performance. Overall, the findings underscore the intricate balance of operational parameters necessary for optimizing PEMFC efficiency.

articleTitle: Direction Estimation and Fault Identification using Superimposed Energy coefficient Technique for the distribution System with distributed Generator
abstract: This paper proposes a new fault identification direction estimation and classification in a modern distribution system. However, the technique is based on super imposed component of energy for each phase in the distribution line. Energy coefficients is a new parameter introduced which can effectively classify the fault and its direction. The energy coefficients scheme is simulated on PSCAD/EMTDC and the results shown in MATLAB which proves the technique is robust, fast and accurate during the disturbances in the system.

articleTitle: Optimizing Power System Performance through Dynamic Line Rating Implementation
abstract: The transmission line plays an important role in ensuring the stability and safety of power grids. The traditional static line ratings (SLR) often set conservative limits based on worst-case scenarios, leading to underutilization of transmission capacity. Dynamic Line Rating (DLR) offers a solution by adjusting capacity dynamically based on real-time weather conditions and conductor temperature data, thereby optimizing transmission efficiency. This paper presents an overview of DLR technology, discussing the heat balance equation as its foundation. Implementation considerations, including capacity calculation and comparison of DLR and SLR based on miniature real-time power system models, are explored. A miniature power system is designed and tested to validate the DLR approach, utilizing real-time data from sensors to dynamically adjust line capacity. Results indicate that DLR offers a significant advantage over SLR, providing higher capacity limits and enhancing transmission efficiency.

articleTitle: Effective EV Battery Charging System Using MPPT Controller for Solar PV System
abstract: The adoption of electric vehicles (EVs) has become more and more popular in the recent years as a way of addressing the issues associated with fossil fuels. Furthermore, the increasing demand in power is addressed by the affiliation of the renewable sources like solar energy at the charging stations. This study utilizes a solar photovoltaic (PV) based EV charging to meet energy demands. The conventional perturb and observe (P&O) MPPT strategy is employed to achieve optimal power production from the solar panel. However, the main disadvantage is the discontinuous nature of operation that PV supplies because of solar irradiation variability. For the purpose of regulating boost and buck modes of bi-directional converters, a closed loop PI (proportional-integral) controller is implemented, employing a constant current and constant voltage (CCCV) approach. The PI controller is suggested to enhance the efficiency of PV power transfer to EV battery storage, guaranteeing optimum usage of PV output and efficient battery charging. The suggested system is developed and executed using MATLAB/Simulink platform. The average PV efficiency, PV power and battery voltage ripple are 98%, 0.065 W and 0.020 V respectively. The outcomes obtained by simulation show that the designed system is adequate for the requiring operation even when there is a variation in solar radiation.

articleTitle: Improving Power Quality Using a PV-Based SEPIC Converter with a Unified Power Flow Controller
abstract: Harmonic reduction techniques in outdated source current systems are defective and unfair when dealing with varying load conditions. These tasks arise from the occurrence of non-linear loads, leading to issues in harmonic mitigation. To address this, filters are engaged to reduce harmonics and improve power quality. Applying these filters for a dynamic response under variable load conditions can be expensive. Enhanced power system security and increased voltage stability under various load conditions are provided by the new Unified Power Flow Controller (UPFC), that features both series and shunt compensating elements. Synchronized Reference Theory (SRF) is working to derive the reference current from the AC source current, making sinusoidal harmonics that respond to load harmonics. This UPFC is proficient in absorbing or injecting reactive power at the PCC. The DC link capacitor's voltage is maintained and raised by the PV system. The Photo Voltaic (PV) array's maximum power can be obtained using the Perturbs & Observe (P&O) MPPT strategy, and then applied to the SEPIC converter to enhance the voltage. D-Q theory, controlled by a hysteresis current controller, produces PWM pulses for the shunt and series compensators. This approach is executed using MATLAB R2021A software.

articleTitle: A Scalable and Secure Cloud Solution for File Management with AWS and EC2
abstract: The service consists of hosting an AWS-based web page application utilizing EC2 instance services. The backend development is done in Java and set up on port 3001 as proprietary REST API using Spring Boot. There is also a provision of installation in order to perform certain specific tasks. Internal files are stored using a self-designed custom file management system, ‘AgiDB’, that utilizes. JSON format due to its simplicity and extensibility. Every admin has an assigned specific folder structure where they are able to update users, create new users, delete users, and view users' information. All users are assigned specific roles, which allows management of user authentication at the admin user, and general user levels. Certain dashboards are shown based on the user’s role by correlating roles and data contained within the ‘userAuthenticator’ directory. Administers have the right to add users, follow or remove users, while normal users have the rights to add, erase, and download files from their folders. The application in the interface ensures that a mobile-friendly layout is maintained through building the frontend on ReactJS. It addresses file management in such a way that the files are synchronized over the cloud hosted on AWS to any device, enhancing ease of management.

articleTitle: Particle Swarm Optimization Based Approximation and Analysis of Boiler System
abstract: The paper attempts to analyze and calculate the approximate of ninth order Boiler system using different technique of order reduction in order to get ease in designing the best suited controller to the actual larger system. The various techniques of order reduction i.e. Differential Method, Stability Preservation Method, Routh Approximation, Balanced truncation method and particle swarm optimization are to be used to find the reduced model of actual boiler system. All time domain parameters are analyzed with the step response of approximates to its actual system and their stability is examined with the bode diagram using MATLAB. PSO is found out to be the best suited technique of order reduction from all the methods discussed in this paper based on their integral square error. This shows the best similar behaviour of the approximated system to the actual boiler system with reduced computational complexity. The paper may be suitable for educating researchers who are involved in the area of order reduction.

articleTitle: A Practical Power Theft Detection System with Simulation and Hardware Implementation
abstract: Power theft remains a persistent challenge for utility providers, leading to significant revenue losses and inefficiencies across power distribution networks. In this paper, a practical and scalable power theft detection system is proposed, utilizing real-time power comparison at multiple points along a distribution line, as well as at individual customer utility points. A Central Monitoring System (CMS) aggregates the data from these locations, enabling the detection of unauthorized power usage and theft.To validate the system's effectiveness, a MATLAB/Simulink simulation model was developed to simulate various power theft scenarios and monitor the system’s detection capabilities. Additionally, a pilot hardware implementation was conducted using microcontroller-based sensors to test part of the system in a real-world environment. The combined results from the simulation and hardware tests demonstrate the system’s accuracy and adaptability, providing a cost-effective and real-time solution for detecting power theft across localized grids. This dual approach of simulation and hardware validation highlights the system’s potential for widespread deployment in both small-scale grids and larger distributed energy networks.

articleTitle: Fractal based Super Broadband mm – Wave Antenna for 5G and Aerospace Applications
abstract: The suggested design is demonstrated for 5G applications from conventional ellipsoid geometry, which is modified further by using sub-elliptical and circular sections, which significantly increase the impedance bandwidth of the antenna in the millimetre wave (mm-wave) spectrum (30–300 GHz). Afterwards, an inverted T-slot etched in the modified W- shaped ground plane extends the wideband to super- wideband/broadband antenna (SWB/SBA) and increases the efficiency of the proposed design geometry. The proposed structure is designed on FR-4 substrate material with a size of 25mm*35mm. The simulation results demonstrate super broadband from 27.30 to 208.23 GHz with a fractional bandwidth (FBW) of 153.64% and a bandwidth ratio (BR) of 7.62 at S11 ≤ -10 db. The designed mm-wave antenna has a radiation efficiency of 60–85% over the broadband range for mm-wave, V-band, W-band, and D-band applications.

articleTitle: Islanding Detection through Intelligent Classifier BI-LSTM Network for Micro Grid
abstract: Every day, additional distributed energy resources (DER)—like solar and wind power systems—are being integrated to keep up with the rising demand for electricity. The integration of distributed generation (DG) offers several technological benefits, including improved power quality, system security, and performance. Apart from the advantages of integrating distributed generation (DG) with the grid, there are certain obstacles that arise because of the decentralized nature of DGs. One of the main problems with DG integration is islanding, which affects equipment, results in poor power quality, and puts utility workers' lives in danger. The Micro Grid's (MG) efficient operation depends on overcoming this speed and accurately detecting islanding, which can be done by putting in place an appropriate islanding detection technique. In this paper intelligent classifier Bidirectional Long Short Term Memory network (BI-LSTM) by using Discrete Wavelet transform (DWT) technique is implemented for the detection of islanding and non-islanding events. Performance accuracy of the proposed classifier can be improved by optimal selection of weights for the classifier which is done by using Particle swarm Optimization algorithm (PSOA). The proposed classifier aims to categorize occurrences that are either islanding or non-islanding under different fault settings. When evaluated with different noise levels, the proposed classifier performed better in terms of Signal Noise Ratio (SNR). When compared to other islanding detection strategies, the MATLAB/Simulink results unmistakably demonstrated that the developed method classified the state of islanding and non-islanding state more accurately.

articleTitle: Design of High-Speed Wallace Tree multiplier Used Full-Adder
abstract: Wallace tree multipliers are an effective solution for achieving power efficiency in high-speed multiplication. By incorporating high-speed 7:3 counters into the Wallace tree reduction process, we can further enhance the speed of the multiplier. In this paper, we introduce an algorithmic method for constructing counter-based Wallace tree multipliers. We provide a comprehensive comparison between traditional Wallace multipliers and their counter-based counterparts, revealing that the counter-based design can be up to 22% faster than its traditional counterpart. Improvements in adder optimization have significantly boosted multiplier performance. We propose a modified full adder that utilizes a multiplexer, aimed at achieving lower power consumption in the multiplier. To evaluate the effectiveness of our design, we reference the conventional Wallace tree multiplier structure. The designs have been developed using Verilog HDL, and their functionalities have been validated through simulation.

articleTitle: Railway Passenger Flow and Sales Prediction Using Advanced Machine Learning Techniques
abstract: Effective passenger waft control is pivotal for the highest quality operation of railway structure, impacting each operational performance and passenger satisfaction. This study delves into the software of system gaining knowledge of strategies to investigate and forecast passenger waft and price tag income inside railway networks. Utilizing historic tour statistics, sensor statistics, and outside influences, we increase predictive fashions that offer treasured insights into passenger conduct and decorate operational decision-making. Our findings spotlight the extensive enhancements in prediction accuracy and operational performance that system gaining knowledge of can deliver, providing sizeable blessings for railway control.

articleTitle: Skin Cancer Classification using Machine Learning Techniques
abstract: The death rate from skin cancer has radically grown due to a lack of understanding about the indications and prevention measures. It is one of the most lethal types of cancers, and the mortality rate due to skin cancer has risen sharply. Cancer must be diagnosed as early as possible to halt its growth and prevent metastasis. Even though there are numerous varieties of skin cancer, melanoma, basal cell carcinoma, and squamous cell carcinoma are considered the three most dangerous types of skin cancer. This research, using the CNN image-processing technology and machine learning, tries to detect and classify into the many kinds of skin cancer. Artificial intelligence (AI) based algorithms for automated skin cancer classification have consistently outperformed human professionals in several clinical studies, laying the groundwork for a future in which AI will be widely used.

articleTitle: Ensembling VGG16 and ResNet50 for Parkinson's Disease Detection Using MRI Dataset
abstract: Early diagnosis of Parkinson’s disease (PD) is notoriously difficult, and no diagnostic methods are reliable. Early diagnosis is essential to improve patient outcomes however, current methods often rely on clinical markers and standard machine learning algorithms to predict the onset of a disease, which are slow and only show moderate success. This project proposes a novel method, for identifying Parkinson’s disease at a nearly stage by applying learning techniques to MRI images. The proposed method takes the best of both architectures i.e., VGG16 and ResNet50 and combine them to improve prediction accuracy. The ensemble model performed better than standalone models with less loss and higher accuracy when training with MRI of the PPMI dataset at an early stage.

articleTitle: Design and Fabrication of Prosthetic Hand
abstract: The design and fabrication of a prosthetic hand using 3D printing technology is presented in this project. This research explores the integration of advanced 3D printing technology in the design and fabrication of a prosthetic hand, aiming to address the limitations of traditional prosthetics. The proposed prosthesis is characterized by its lightweight, customizable, and cost-effective nature, utilizing additive manufacturing techniques to optimize functionality and aesthetics. The design process involves the use of computer-aided design (CAD) software to create a biomimetic hand model, considering both anatomical accuracy and user comfort.

articleTitle: Efficient battery management using cell balancing techniques
abstract: A vital component of battery management systems for electric vehicles (EVs) is cell balancing, which maintains consistent charge levels in each cell to maximize efficiency, prolong battery life, and improve safety. Cell voltage imbalances are effectively addressed by using both active and passive balancing approaches. Active cell balancing is the process of dividing up the energy amongst the cells by transferring surplus charge from higher voltage cells to lower voltage cells using external electronics, such as resistors or transformers. Accurate voltage control is made possible by this technique, which works especially well with large battery packs. Conversely, passive balancing uses dissipative components to balance cell voltages by releasing surplus energy as heat, such as resistors or capacitors. Passive cell balancing is less effective and might not be appropriate for high-power or big voltage differential applications, despite being easier to use and less expensive. Both approaches, in spite of their distinctions, are essential for preserving cell integrity, reducing deterioration, and improving battery performance in electric vehicles. To maximize energy efficiency, guarantee dependability, and increase the longevity of EV batteries, these methods must be integrated into battery management systems. This will enable the automotive industry to deploy electric vehicles more widely.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of 1Dimensional CNN and LSTM Deep Learning Approaches in Speech Depression Detection
abstract: Detecting depression is critical for early intervention, preventing degradation in mental health and improving overall quality of life. Speech depression is difficult to identify for non-invasive, real-time monitoring due to variability in speech patterns and minor depressive signs. This study analyses the effectiveness of two key deep learning algorithms, a Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) and a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN), utilized for speech emotion recognition, thereby identifying negative emotions that can lead to depression. The publicly available, fairly balanced dataset RAVDESS is adopted to evaluate the generalization powers of the models. Following data augmentation, MFCC features were extracted and fed into both networks. Although both models reached similar training accuracy levels, the generalization capability of the CNN on unseen testing data notably surpassed that of the LSTM, achieving 83% in contrast to 59%.

articleTitle: Design and Development of Smart Seed Dispenser for Efficient Cultivation
abstract: The advancement in technology gifted the cultivation sector of agriculture field with many automation systems. In smart cultivation, the efficiency of cultivation could be improved with a seed dispenser system. Seed dispenser plays a vital role in productive cultivation of crops in the farming field at any weather. The smart seed dispenser aims to reduce the human effort, time, and labor cost of cultivation while simultaneously increasing the productivity and efficiency of farming. This work delves into the design and development of a prototype of a seed dispenser system on top of a mobile controlled vehicle. The designed system can autonomously perform the tasks of plowing, sowing and levelling in the agricultural field. It is observed that uniformity in seed size enhances both the consistency and effectiveness of the dispensing rate. Practical analysis of the designed prototype is performed to dispense the seed remotely using smartphone. The results demonstrate improved accuracy, time efficiency, and overall effectiveness in cultivation compared to conventional techniques.

articleTitle: Feasibility and Economic Evaluation of Thermoelectric Generator (TEG) Module for Rural Electrification
abstract: In order to search how to fetch electricity to rural areas in India, which are not connected to the main power grid system by using the technology that is Thermoelectric generator (TEG). The project surveys the cost effectiveness and practical uses of TEGs system in rural areas. This include looking at the expenses involved in establishment and maintenance of the generating system as well as whether this system can able to generate enough power for the people’s daily needs in their areas. If the system appears to be an economical and reliable option, they could help to get sustainable power to off-grid community in India. Main objective of the system is to generate at least 60 watts of power which is enough for a 9-watt bulb for 8 hours at night. The project takes a look at ways to make TEG system more affordable. It examines factors like how effectively system work, the handiness of biomass in local area to provide heat and lesser costs for the system settings. The system would take 136 years to pay back the total investment, which is quite impractical in places where there is already access to the main power grid. It can be a good solution for the rural areas without reliable electricity. For making TEG system more practical, the study also search ideas like combining the system with other power source which act as hybrid system, emplacing then at community level and financial support of government to reduce the cost. The long-term durableness, reliability and environmental sustainability of the system makes this system a good choice for fulfill the energy needs of India’s remote area.

articleTitle: Empirical Evaluation of License Plate Recognition Using Tensorflow Framework
abstract: Due to the tremendous increase in vehicles, more attention is required to Intelligent Transport Systems (ITS). License Plate Recognition (LPR) is one such method in ITS. Although there are several researches on LPR, still the issues are partially solved. This is because license plate images suffer from low illumination, side view, etc. This paper developed a method to recognize license plates. It consists of license plate localization, segmentation and recognition. A Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) is designed for recognition. The proposed method is tested on the Chinese City Parking Dataset (CCPD), Chinese License Plate Dataset (CLPD), Application Oriented License Plate (AOLP) and PKUData datasets. The performance of the proposed LPR method is evaluated using accuracy. It outperforms other recent methods by achieving an accuracy of 95%

articleTitle: Advancements in Highway Navigation System Using Light Based Technology
abstract: In the realm of heightened concern over the number of traffic accidents and the casualties they cause, communication-based vehicle safety applications have surfaced as one of the most effective ways to improve road safety. In this domain, visible light communications (VLC) hold a significant potential attribute which include its broad coverage, efficiency, and straightforward design. A bidirectional wireless technology called Li-Fi (light fidelity) uses LED or infrared light to transfer data. To send an internet signal using light waves, Li-Fi technology just requires a light source equipped with a chip. The main motive is to achieve precise and accurate navigation details in a highway while travelling in an automotive vehicle when the traveler faces issues like inaccuracy in vehicles GPS, low network connectivity and also to avoid traffic congestion using light fidelity technology (Li-Fi). In comparison to Wi-Fi, it provides more bandwidth, efficiency, availability, and security, and in lab settings, it exhibits amazing speeds. Li-Fi, which takes use of light's increased speed, is a major improvement over current data transfer method. Additionally, this project outlines potential future research avenues for automotive VLC applications and offers a brief overview of related standardization efforts. The primary aim is to highlight the significant potential of VLC and to facilitate its effective implementation in enhancing road safety.

articleTitle: Enhancing Potato Leaf Disease Detection: A Comparative Study of CNN Architectures with K-means Segmentation and Data Augmentation
abstract: Potato, the third most consumed crop globally, faces significant challenges from leaf diseases. This research proposes an automated deep learning system for detecting and classifying potato leaf diseases. Utilizing computer vision techniques, the study evaluated three CNN architectures (VGG19, VGG16, ResNet50) on a 2,580-image dataset. The VGG16 model, enhanced with K-means segmentation and data augmentation, achieved 97.1% accuracy in identifying healthy and blight-infected leaves. Proposed GAN-based data enhancement further improved performance to 98.2%. By integrating advanced image processing and machine learning, the approach offers a promising solution for early disease detection, enabling farmers to implement timely crop management interventions.

articleTitle: Development of a Prosthetic Leg for Driving Incorporating EMG Sensor Technology
abstract: The prosthetic legs that have become available recently are substantially better, despite their complexity. Unfortunately, the majority of people cannot afford them due to their expensive pricing. Even though low-cost fixed prostheses are available, they only allow very rudimentary movement with an unnatural stride, making driving a vehicle difficult using those legs. This paper outlines approaches for designing an Electromyography-based prototype prosthetic leg that mimics actual human leg movements. Since current prosthetic devices have limited mobility and are prohibitively expensive, the primary objective of this research is to design a cost-effective prosthetic human leg suitable for driving. The design incorporates the use of an Electromyography sensor for high mobility, which is uncommon in commercial products. This research will provide a foundation for further efforts in prosthetic creations.

articleTitle: Enhanced Water Quality Classification: Advanced Gradient-Boosting Ensembles for Sustainable Environmental Management
abstract: The water quality influences public health and environmental sustainability, and increased levels of pollution demand far more efficient methods of measurement and classification. This article applies machine learning algorithms; namely, CatBoost, XGBoost, and LGBoost, in a weighted voting ensemble for the classification of water quality across various safety levels. The ensemble approach achieved the highest accuracy at 94.37 per cent, overtaking individual models such as CatBoost at 93.97 per cent and XGBoost at 93.45 per cent. Cross-validation results showed slight variations in the results, showing how stable the ensemble model is when different subsets of data are used. Hence, these results point to the benefit of using ensemble techniques that enhance predictive accuracy by balancing the strengths of each model. This study demonstrates the efficacy of ensemble methods for reliable water quality classification and provides a foundation for scalable environmental monitoring solutions. This approach may facilitate continuous, AI-driven water quality assessments, which can provide timely insights into sustainable water resource management.

articleTitle: A novel method of Detection of Hot spots in Solar Panels using Deep learning-based Object Detection Algorithm
abstract: The formation of hot spots in solar panels is a critical aspect of a photovoltaic system. These anomalies can significantly affect the efficiency and longevity of the panels. In this paper, a deep learning-based objection detection algorithm is used to detect the hot spots in solar panels in a more efficient and easy way. The hotspot dataset is collected using a thermal camera from installed solar panels of BIT Sindri, Dhanbad. The thermal images are manually annotated using Roboflow. The mean average precision (mAP) for the different classes of hotspot achieved a satisfactory result. The object detection technique YOLO has proven highly responsive, highlighting its suitability for practical use for preventative maintenance of photovoltaic panels.

articleTitle: Hybrid Computational Intelligent Techniques for Electrical Load Forecasting
abstract: The goal of Electrical load forecasting is to estimate future electrical load in order to maximize power system efficiency and preserve supply and demand balance. With the use of fuzzy logic and artificial neural networks, we have implemented hybrid intelligence known as CANFIS. Addressing the growing complexity and accuracy requirements in electrical load prediction is the driving force behind the project "Hybrid Computational Intelligent Techniques for Electrical Load Forecasting". The main advantage is that it aids in preventing an excess or a shortfall of electricity. Fuzzy logic and neural networks are used in the coactive neuro fuzzy inference to provide strong computational intelligence. Weights are adjusted by the Delta Bar Delta rule and Bell membership function is being used. We have compared CANFIS with Radial basis function network and Exponential Smoothing.

Author Keywords: CANFIS With Bell Membership Function and Delta-Bar- Delta Learning

articleTitle: Innovative Hybrid Strategy for Order Reduction of Linear System and DC Motor Speed Control
abstract: The work presented here Proposed a hybrid method for the reduction of order in linear systems. In this presented hybrid method, aspects from the traditional method and an optimization method developed recently have been adopted on high order system (HOS) order reduction. This Combined method has been applied to two HOS. The numerator coefficients of the Reduced System (RS) are computed using the Arithmetic Optimization Algorithm (AOA) and the denominator coefficients of the RS are obtained using the Stability Equation Method (SEM) while using ISE as an Objective Function for order reduction to diminish the variance among the HOS and the Proposed RS. The performance parameters have been estimated using the Proposed hybrid method and compared with the existing method. Using the Proposed Method, Transient Parameters are also estimated and compared with the other methods. The Proposed RS showed very high accuracy in comparison with the existing methods. Furthermore, the use of an AOA application with the Proportional Integral Derivative (PID) controller has been employed for controlling the speed of the DC motor and the Objective Function adopted in this work was Integral of Time Absolute Error (ITAE).

articleTitle: Harnessing Wind Power for On-the-Go Device Charging: The Portable Mobile Charger Revolution
abstract: Wind energy based small scale electricity generator for home appliances is very important. Nowadays mobile phones are essential devices for people, but today also there is the problem of charging phones when their power is off or while traveling from a vehicle it is not possible to charge the phones. This paper presents the design and implementation of VAWT which is a small and helical twisted Savonius VAWT, which is able to charge phones where there is no power. This system includes VAWT and dynamo which will take power from the turbine and be able to produce up to 5 Volt depending on RPM. Due to the twisting of turbine blades and end plates that attach at the upper and lower end the system gives good performance. The main approach of the system is to implement the concept of area convergence. In the proposed system area is converged in such a way that wind will come from a large area and reach the turbine through a small area so as the area decreases the velocity of wind increases and so power output of the wind turbine also increases. In this way, the whole integrated device will be able to produce the desired amount of voltage and current so that we can charge our phones. This is the green energy for mobile phones if there is no utility supply.

articleTitle: Enhancing Dynamic Performance of Grid Tied Wind Turbine using ADRC based STATCOM
abstract: Power system stability is substantially impacted when wind farms are disconnected from grid network in unusual grid scenarios. To augment the dynamic performance of grid-tied wind turbine systems, this study proposes a robust Active Disturbance Rejection Control (ADRC) for STATCOM. To augment the performance of the wind turbine, in addition to accounting for external grid disruptions, the suggested scheme also calculates and eliminates internal parameter changes, parameter uncertainties, and cross coupling factors. The suggested control scheme effectiveness is explained through comparisons with the vector PI control method, assessed under both balanced and unbalanced fault conditions in MATLAB/Simulink. The outcomes show that existing approach substantially shows better performance than the conventional scheme in handling these fault scenarios. Moreover, it enhances Low Voltage Ride-Through (LVRT) capability of wind energy systems in weak grid conditions, offering better performance than the traditional vector control method.

articleTitle: Using Fuzzy Set Theory for Adaptive, Dynamic Recommendations in Social Media Platforms
abstract: Adaptive and dynamic social media site recommendations are described as the continuous alteration of suggested content in accordance with actual, real-time interaction of users and shifting preference so that just what they need may be discovered at their very own time. This paper seeks to explore fuzzy set theory for further improvement in recommendation systems on social media sites at the wake of uncertainty and dynamic user preferences. Unlike the traditional approaches utilizing deterministic algorithms, fuzzy set theory allows modeling partial and ambiguous user interests with the help of degrees of membership, which finds application in the handling of the complexities of social media behavior. The proposed framework, therefore, employs fuzzy rules to create adaptive and dynamic recommendations that are updated continuously by real-time user interaction and emerging trends. Multiple criteria such as engagement, levels of activity, and inferred preferences are used in fuzzy inference systems to evaluate content relevance, whereby it can suggest content with a flexible, yet integrative approach. Adaptive learning is expected to facilitate the continuous refinement of membership functions and rule bases so that recommendations stay on track and aligned with the evolution of user's interests. Thus, this research thus captures the success of incorporating fuzzy set theory in social media recommendations. These have improved the accuracy of personalized content delivery, user satisfaction, and boosting engagements. Based on the paper, the mathematical foundations, system architecture, and performance benefits are outlined; and the power of fuzzy logic is depicted as it forms a powerful tool for future-proofing next-generation recommendation systems.

articleTitle: Optimizing Athletic Performance through Nutrition and Machine Learning: A Comprehensive Review
abstract: Nutrition plays a pivotal function in athletic general overall performance, influencing training, competition, and healing. This paper examines the influence of macronutrients (proteins, carbohydrates, fats), micronutrients (vitamins, minerals), and hydration on general overall performance, integrating insights from sports activities sports era and device learning. Recent advances in periodized vitamins and personalized dietary strategies are more with the resource of the use of wearable generation and information analytics, providing real- time monitoring and optimization of athletes` nutritional status. Current evidence on dietary nutritional dietary supplements for enhancing general overall performance and healing is reviewed. Findings emphasize the importance of tailored vitamins plans based totally mostly on sport-precise wishes and character wishes. Practical pointers for optimizing general overall performance thru strategic vitamins and leveraging device learning tools are provided, underscoring vitamin’s vital function in maximizing athletic capability and long-term health.

articleTitle: Advanced Hybrid Energy Storage System with Integrated Battery and Supercapacitor Technology
abstract: A Battery and Supercapacitor Hybrid Energy Storage Systems (B-SHESS) performance, dependability, and longevity are all intended to be improved by increasing its energy efficiency. High-energy-density batteries and supercapacitors can be combined to the system combines substantial energy storage with rapid power delivery. Our approach includes developing a comprehensive dynamic simulation model to predict system performance across various conditions. Key performance metrics such as energy efficiency, power levels, cycle life, and response time will be rigorously tested and validated through empirical methods and HESS. Successful implementation of this project is expected to advance hybrid energy storage technologies, significantly enhancing energy efficiency in applications like electric vehicles, renewable energy systems, and grid stabilization, thereby contributing to more sustainable and efficient energy solutions.

articleTitle: Enhancing Organ Donor Matching and Transparency with Blockchain Technology
abstract: Organ transplant is a life-saving treatment, but issues like privacy of data, transparency and fair distribution act as barriers. Most of the current systems are based on centralized repositories and manual processes that pose risks to privacy and are also inefficient. In this paper, we propose a blockchain-based solution for securing donor and receiver information in a permissioned-blockchain-network. Smart contracts facilitate organ allocation based on defined parameters that make the process more transparent while considering fairness. Encryption helps ensure security from unauthorized access by encrypting sensitive data which enables secure organ allocation — handling the data storage and retrieval management challenges also effectively. Performance evaluation using synthetic data reveals that our proposed approach handles authentic organ request allocation securely for nearly 30% more recipients with similar/less CPU time compared to other approaches thus making it more effective in live scenario implementations.

articleTitle: Fractional-Order PI controller based Field-Oriented Controller for PMSM
abstract: The Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor (PMSM) mathematical model, which is often referred to as a sinusoidal Brushless DC (BLDC) motor, has highly nonlinear characteristics. A cascade control structure, which comprises of an inner current control loop and an outer speed control loop, is commonly employed to regulate the speed of this motor. This work proposes a fractional-order proportional-integral (PI) controller-based field oriented control system for torque and speed control of PMSMs. This approach achieves a constant torque angle by keeping the direct-axis current. Three PI controllers are primarily needed for this method: one to maintain the direct-axis current at zero, one to maintain the quadrature axis current at maximum, and one to maintain the speed at the reference level. According to the simulation results, the suggested approach outperforms the traditional method in terms of overshoot and fast dynamic responsiveness.

articleTitle: Intelligent Fault Pattern Recognition in Electric Vehicles Using Machine Learning
abstract: Electric Vehicles also berred as EVs becoming more popular, because of its environmentally beneficial attributes and the latest developments in automotive technology. A machine learning-based fault detection system tailored for Electric Vehicles (EVs) is presented in this study. It can perform predictive maintenance, failure identification. This method improves EV operations dependability, safety, and efficiency by using a dataset with six categories: one for normal operation and five for different types of faults. It seeks to avoid unplanned break downs and reduce maintenance expenses. Nonetheless,difficulties like the risk of overfitting, the computational requirements of machine learning models, and the availability of high-quality labeled datasets are recognized. A deployment platform such as MATLAB facilitates the installation of this intelligent fault detection system, guaranteeing efficient monitoring of internal vehicle components.The overall goal of this research is to increase EV operational reliability by implementing better safety and maintenance procedures.

articleTitle: Predictive Modeling of Shear Capacity for FRCM-Strengthened RC Beams using MLP Neural Networks and Global Sensitivity Analysis for Sustainable Construction
abstract: This work, focuses on the development and prediction ability assessment of a multilayer perceptron (MLP) neural network model to forecast the FRCM-RC beam’s shear strength. The dataset includes 89 samples of the experiment and has been pre-processed with the MinMax Scaling for better model convergence. The MLP model again demonstrates quite robust performance, reaching a high R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> score of 0.938, which is yet more indicative of this model’s capability to cover 93.8% of shear capacity variability. The accuracy of the model was further validated by model evaluation metrics: MSE, RMSE, MAE, and MAPE. An Actual vs Predicted plot was further used to substantiate this. Global sensitivity analysis pointed out that the highly important role of reinforcement ratios (ρ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">l</inf>, ρ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">w</inf>, ρ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">f</inf>, ρ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">cm</inf>) on predictions of shear capacity is brought towards valuable insight to optimization. This study would, therefore, provide a reliable predictive tool for engineers to further enhance the understanding and improvements to FRCM-strengthened RC beam design.

articleTitle: Controlling Power Production in Isolated Electrical Systems Using Superconducting Magnetic Energy Storage and an Artificial Electric Field Algorithm
abstract: Complex control methods are required to keep power networks stable and operate smoothly as they integrate more energy sources and power generating units. In this study, the examined system consists of wind unit, diesel generator unit, gas turbine unit, and solar unit integrating superconducting energy storage in meeting renewable sources and shifting demand patterns improves the system frequency stability. For minimizing load variation, PID controller optimizes the controlled generation units using artificial electric field algorithm. This study used time-weighted error integration to evaluate the flexibility and efficacy of this algorithm and demonstrates how efficiently control the power supply.

articleTitle: Optimizing Frequency Stability in Autonomous Power System Using the Artificial Electric Field Algorithm with Electric Vehicle
abstract: Electric vehicles (EVs) are a potential mode of mobility for the future. When EVs are linked to the power grid, uncertainties cause power-system frequency issues. The LFC in an HPS with EVs was the focus of this study. The CCGT, DEG, WTG, and solar PV units comprise an isolated HPS (IHPS). Integrating superconducting magnetic energy storage technology ensures power supply and system reliability. A PID controller improves the EV performance. The PID controller manages the WTG, CCGT, and DEG for load-frequency management. These controllers were set using the artificial electric field method. This study tests the IHPS model under perturbation method.

articleTitle: Software Based Self Determined Welfare Scheme
abstract: The innovative web program known as the Software-Based Self-Determined Welfare Scheme aims to completely transform the welfare benefit application process. Without the need for laborious paperwork or drawn-out bureaucratic processes, users can easily register online and ask for social aid directly through this site. In order to expedite the application process and guarantee that aid reaches the most deserving recipients, users of the website can register and provide vital personal information as well as financial situation details. This innovative web application empowers users by putting them in control of their welfare journey, offering a user-friendly interface to navigate through the application process with ease. With secure authentication protocols in place, users can trust that their information is kept confidential throughout the registration and application process. By leveraging the power of technology, this software-based welfare scheme not only enhances accessibility and efficiency but also promotes transparency and accountability in the distribution of welfare benefits, ultimately empowering individuals to take charge of their own welfare need.

articleTitle: Voice-Controlled Home Automation using VC-02 module
abstract: This paper introduces a voice controlled home automation using the VC-02 module. It aims to make it easier and more accessible to manage household devices. By connecting the VC-02 to 4 channel relay, the system provides an easy way to automate home appliances without requiring complicated programming or extra equipment. People can utilize their devices without physical interaction through voice control. This creates a simpler and easier way for them to interact with their homes. This new way of using home technology makes everyday tasks easier and shows how it can make life better in different places, like smart homes and care facilities.

articleTitle: Localized Open-Source LLM Aware Retrieval Augmented Generation of Legal Documents: A Case Study on Indian Constitution and Penal Code
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are advanced artificial intelligence systems which are designed to generate human-like language based on their training data. Retrieval- Augmented Generation (RAG) is a framework that enhances the response of LLM by incorporating external information sources, leading to more accurate, context-relevant responses. However, LLMs commonly struggle with contextual relevance, especially in particular fields such as legal documentation, where specific local laws are crucial. Furthermore, there is limited research on the use of RAG technology in the legal area, particularly for producing and analyzing legal documents. This study develops a chatbot using RAG to answer questions on the Indian Constitution (IC) and the Indian Penal Code (IPC), with a Streamlit-based interface to display legal queries and their generated responses. This study analyzes the evaluation of various LLMs integrated with RAG including (including (i) Llama3 8b, (ii) Mistral 7b, (iii) Gemma2 7b, (iv) Phi3 3.8b, and (v) Qwen2 7b and it evaluates their performance in terms of relevance, faithfulness, context recall, and context precision.

articleTitle: A Comprehensive Hybrid CNN-LSTM Deep Learning Model for Accurate Landslide Prediction
abstract: A significant natural threat, landslides take lives and damage infrastructure. Economic setbacks often follow. The complex interplay of external factors-like terrain attributes and data on climate-has made detecting slides a big challenge with traditional forecasting methods. This research constitutes a hybrid deep framework deploying Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) for space data handling and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks for analyzing temporal data. The hybrid model utilizes satellite imagery and temporal data from weather events to enhance the accuracy of landscape detection. The model has made use of data and regularization to prepare the system for generalization. To exemplify the performance of the proposed system, the model was tested using a number of performance metrics, such as an accuracy rate, precision, and recall. With a model accuracy of 94%, the results are promising compared to conventional methods, thus showing the system to be a reliable solution for real-time landslide prediction systems.

articleTitle: An Android Malware Detection Approach Based On SIMGRU
abstract: In the current world, malware poses a threat to security due to its extraordinary proliferation in the wake of the Internet’s rapid expansion in recent years. The purpose of this essay is to describe SIM GRU as a standard detection tool for Android malware. When doing a static analysis of Android malware, clustered similarity is frequently employed. In this manner, we demonstrate the similarities between the improvement of the Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU) and obtain three Sim GRU variants: InputSimGRU, HiddenSimGRU, and InputHiddenSimGRU. Combining InputSimGRU with the Hid-denSimGRU and it results in InputHiddenSimGRU.Experiments display that InputSimGRU, InputHiddenSimGRU, and Hidden-SimGRU perform finer than the GRU model and alternative techniques.

articleTitle: Deep Sentiment Analysis Methods using Machine Learning for Extraction of Brand Value for Various Consumer Products
abstract: This research produces an extensive multilingual data mining sentiment analysis model. Utilizing the material obtained, such as consumer reviews as well as on social networking sites, partial impacts, the use of local language that might influence output have been prevented to some level by limitation. Also included are stepdown of using emojis in words and use of characters as well as expressions by quantification toward assessing strength toward sentiments. Using feature extraction and context creation through domain-specific sentiment analysis, intricate viewpoints are captured. Thus, it classifies for improving the accuracy of sentiment detection due to the application of complex machine learning techniques. Through an attempt to provide an adequate framework for evaluating brand value across a range of consumer products, this model amalgamates domain-specific knowledge with cooperative sentiment extraction methods. It will help organizations better understand public sentiment and enhance their decision-making procedures in the long run.

articleTitle: Skin Lession Classification using Deep EnsembleNet
abstract: Although biopsies have been the standard evaluating metric, specialist rely on pattern and symptoms to make final decision for evaluating skin cancer. Increasing cases of skin cancer and less specialist can impact a lot on the detection. Recently, Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) have emerged as an efficient tool to assist the physician in decision making. Transfer learning is now possible with a large number of pre-trained CNN models. It is frequently necessary to adjust input to suit the input layers in order to use these models. There is quite mismatch between the skin lesion image size and the input layer of different pre-trained models. Resizing corrects the size mismatch; however, it may unintentionally eliminate important characteristics required for precise categorisation. We provide a new EnsembleNet with base MobileNet for the early detection of skin lesions such as nevus and melanoma. Making patches of pictures for input instead of whole picture for classification is being investigated using this method. Also, the other models like denseNet, EfficientNet, ResNet, VGG and Xception Net are studied for the accuracy and loss comparison.

articleTitle: Reliability and Efficiency Analysis of Liquid Cooling for Lithium-Ion Batteries in Electric Vehicles
abstract: Electric vehicles (EVs) have emerged as a popular topic of interest for governments and manufacturers amid mounting concerns regarding energy scarcity and pollution. Management of the thermal load that is produced during the process of charging and discharging of batteries, however, is a substantial obstacle. Liquid cooling has demonstrated potential as an effective approach to managing the temperature of electric vehicle batteries. Furthermore, the design, manufacturing, and efficacy of electric vehicles are significantly influenced by their reliability. The reliability of liquid cooling in improving the performance of electric vehicles (EVs) is evaluated in this article using a Markov model and MATLAB simulations.

articleTitle: Integrating IOT for Helmet to Enhanced Safety and Connectivity
abstract: A growing concern over the safety of roads, particularly for riders on two-wheelers has necessitated creation of innovative approaches aimed at avoiding accidents and reducing their consequences. The project is aimed at introducing a Smart Helmet that comes with advanced sensing technology to recognize accidents as soon as they happen and to call emergency services immediately in order to assist afflicted riders. For detecting strong impact during an accident, the helmet has a built-in vibration sensor. With a loose surface beneath them when they lose control, GPS picks up the point of the mishap and uses GSM to send the district-based messages to next available police stations or hospitals soonest possible. The smart system is based on the integration of other detection tools like vibration sensor, A9G board also accelerometer which form basis for fast and accurate response techniques.

articleTitle: Design and Performance Analysis of Vertiwind Power Generation by Radial Axis Permanent Magnet Generator
